topics.topic: Constitutional Democracy: Separation of powers, checks and balances, and judicial review
learningObjectives: Explain Montesquieu’s doctrine of separation of powers among the three arms of government
Illustrate mechanisms of checks and balances in Nigeria’s presidential system
Define judicial review and its supremacy in curbing legislative and executive excesses

topics.topic: Electoral System in Nigeria: INEC mandate, voter registration, and electronic voting (BVAS/IReV)
learningObjectives: Detail the constitutional mandate of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
Explain the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) process and issuance of PVCs
Analyze modern electoral technologies: Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and IReV portal

topics.topic: Electoral Malpractices: Vote buying, ballot snatching, intimidation, and preventive reforms
learningObjectives: Categorize pre-election, election day, and post-election malpractices in Nigeria
Examine the socio-economic causes and consequences of commercialized vote-buying ('stomach infrastructure')
Propose institutional reforms to secure polling units and safeguard election sanctity

topics.topic: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs): Roles in democracy, human rights, and policy advocacy
learningObjectives: Define Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
Highlight CSO contributions to election observation, anti-corruption, and women empowerment
Evaluate challenges faced by civil society: funding constraints and state intimidation

topics.topic: Public Service Reforms: SERVICOM, IPPIS, Due Process, and Whistleblower Policy
learningObjectives: Explain the founding principles of SERVICOM (Service Compact with All Nigerians)
Analyze the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System (IPPIS) in ghost worker elimination
Examine the Bureau of Public Procurement (Due Process) in ensuring transparency in government contracts

topics.topic: National Security and Emerging Security Threats: Terrorism, banditry, and cybercrime
learningObjectives: Define national security and explain the interplay between human security and military defense
Analyze root causes of violent extremism, banditry, kidnapping, and pipeline vandalism in Nigeria
Highlight statutory provisions of the Cybercrimes Act of 2015 and citizen reporting responsibilities

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Mock Electoral Tribunal Simulation
learningObjectives: Assess student comprehension of electoral processes, CSOs, and national security challenges
Conduct a simulated Election Petition Tribunal demonstrating evidence presentation and legal adjudication
Provide corrective tutoring on the operational functions of BVAS and SERVICOM

topics.topic: International Human Rights Instruments: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948)
learningObjectives: Trace the historical origin of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) by the United Nations
Analyze key articles safeguarding civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights
Evaluate the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights and its domestication in Nigerian law

topics.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy Principles: Non-alignment, Afrocentrism, and ECOWAS leadership
learningObjectives: Identify core pillars of Nigeria’s foreign policy since independence in 1960
Explain Africa as the center-piece of Nigerian foreign diplomacy (liberation struggles, anti-apartheid)
Examine Nigeria's leading role in ECOWAS, ECOMOG peacekeeping missions, and the African Union

topics.topic: Environmental Sanitation, Climate Change, and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
learningObjectives: Analyze environmental degradation in Nigeria: desertification in the North, erosion in the East, oil pollution in the Delta
Explain the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework
Advocate for personal and community eco-friendly habits (tree planting, plastic recycling, clean energy)

topics.topic: National Ethics and the National Orientation Agency (NOA) Mandate
learningObjectives: Enumerate national core values under Section 23 of the 1999 Constitution (discipline, integrity, social justice)
Evaluate campaigns of the National Orientation Agency (NOA) in fostering civic orientation
Promote active citizenship, self-reliance, and zero tolerance for corrupt practices

topics.topic: Comprehensive WASSCE/NECO Civic Education Revision & Past Paper Marathon
learningObjectives: Review entire senior secondary civic education syllabus spanning governance, rights, and international relations
Execute timed speed drills on 50 objective questions and structured theory essays
Coach candidates on answering multi-part questions to maximize marks in WAEC Paper 2

topics.topic: Terminal Mock Examination and Broadsheet Entry
learningObjectives: Administer standardized mock WASSCE Civic Education examination
Score scripts strictly according to WAEC criteria and rubric guidelines
Record and certify final continuous assessment scores for graduation transcripts
